fields.v: Benchmark construction: repository mining (filters, in-depth search, expert review) -> task construction (Docker environment pinned at source version, future history pruned; roadmap from release narratives and diffs; tests adapted from upstream; gold patch) -> static validation (compliance, target-level instruction-test alignment, oracle revalidation) -> rollout-based quality control (agents of three tiers, attribution of failures to task or model, repair). Evaluation: agent implements the roadmap in the source-version snapshot within 2 h, then weighted per-target tests

Repetitions: single trial per model. Human intervention: none during runs

fields.v: Claude-Opus-4.7 best (39.1% resolved, 0.692 CS), then Claude-Opus-4.6 (32.2%) and GPT-5.4 (29.6%); others 5.2%-20.9%. Completion Score always higher than resolved rate (partial progress common). ML & Data hardest, ORM & Validation more tractable, UI & Rendering widest spread (Opus-4.7 64.3%). Resolved rate falls with files, lines and number of targets. Stronger models explore less (Opus-4.7 35% Explore, about 101 tool calls) and convert steps into edits; GLM-5.1 uses more steps (163 vs 140) for 20 pp less. Scaffold: top models robust (Opus-4.6 0.9 pp difference), mid/lower tiers swing 3-10 pp; OpenHands better for most (DeepSeek-V4-Pro +7.9 pp, MiniMax-M2.7 +6.1 pp), Terminus 2 better for GLM-5.1 (+2.6 pp) and Qwen3.6-Plus (+4.3 pp). Failures shift from Implementation Error (strong models) to Build Error and Missing Implementation (weak models). No significance tests between models

fields.v: Only two scaffolds (OpenHands, Terminus 2); performance is scaffold-sensitive. Tests verify behaviour but not code quality, maintainability or idiomatic style; multi-dimensional metrics are future work. Limited subset of ecosystems despite 5 languages. Gap: long-horizon multi-target software development remains largely unsolved; failures occur at integration, correctness and construction-level reliability

fields.v: Inconsistencies: text says in ML & Data 'six of thirteen models resolve no tasks' and 'only the top three exceed 8%' (p. 8), but Table 2 (p. 7) shows 0.0% for three models under OpenHands (Kimi-K2.5, Qwen3.5-397B, Seed-2.0-Pro; six zeros only when both scaffolds are counted) and 8.3% for four further models; Opus-4.7 averages 101 tool calls in §5.2 text and 102 in Figure 6(b); post-QC Terminus scores in Appendix Table 4 (p. 23: Claude-Opus-4.6 30.4% / 0.683, GLM-5.1 20.4% / 0.511, Kimi-K2.5 7.1% / 0.348) differ from Table 2 Terminus rows (31.3% / 0.666, 20.9% / 0.512, 7.8% / 0.360); Appendix G.1 (p. 21) lists the five target languages as Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, but the benchmark contains C++ (Glaze, thread-pool) and no Java (Table 3, p. 16); §5.4 (p. 10) says GLM-5.1 and Qwen3.6-Plus are 'the only exceptions' doing better on Terminus 2 and that mid/lower-tier models swing 3-10 pp, but Table 2 (p. 7) also shows Kimi-K2.6 (15.7% vs 14.8%) and Qwen3.5-397B (10.4% vs 9.6%) higher on Terminus 2, with swings below 1 pp. Values taken from Table 2. Quality control used agents of three capability tiers and kept only tasks where tiers score differently, which can shape the benchmark towards the models used; Appendix Table 4 suggests these were Claude-Opus-4.6, GLM-5.1 and Kimi-K2.5 under Terminus 2, which are also evaluated models (not stated explicitly). Iterative QC: 45 of 115 tasks needed at least one fix round (average 3.1 rounds). Static review by experts assisted by Claude-Opus-4.7. Repository identities and versions anonymized in instructions. Code (github.com/UniPat-AI/RoadmapBench), dataset (HuggingFace UnipatAI/RoadmapBench) and leaderboard released. No pre-registration. Languages: Python, TypeScript, C++, Go, Rust
